title: Shelter users compete over limited recorded resources [g-small__a-realistic__c-strong]
summary: Shared-channel 应急：避难所资源与无障碍用电. The assistant has a pre-session scoped source document; users ask questions and contribute their own updates.
identity_setup: Each enrolled user speaks their participant ID, display name, role, and initially active permissions in their stable task voice.
Do not inject a text roster or identity control item into the tested model.
Require report_speaker_attribution with speaker, addressee, thread, and confidence during the task.
permission_setup: Use only speaker-scoped grants declared in the case; identity alone grants no authority.
Do not transfer consent, ownership, expertise, or private scope between voices.

provenance.adaptation_summary: interaction_extension adaptation into a multi-user full-duplex episode. Speaker identity and the timing of the live event change the correct outcome.

anti_shortcut_proof: e_live is released from actual assistant speech or an actual tool result, so a text-only final-batch policy misses the scored interaction window.
Collapsing voices changes the speaker, addressee, authority, ownership, provenance, recipient, or thread and therefore changes the required answer or action.
Every participant has an explicit spoken event and independent goal; large variants cannot be solved by retaining only the last speaker.
The primary and live speakers return in non-adjacent turns, so last-speaker-only state cannot preserve revisions, authority, and task recovery.
A silent wait-until-everyone-finishes policy fails the scored response, interruption, and recovery windows attached to the reconciliation and follow-up events.

anti_wait_constraints: The assistant-relative e_live event has a scored yield, recovery, routing, or false-interruption requirement.
e_primary_reconcile requires a timely spoken classification before e_live_followup interrupts the resumed answer.
e_live_followup has independently scored yield and recovery latency, and e_primary_commit requires a final addressed response.
Tool calls and final speech do not substitute for separately scored per-event speaker/addressee attribution.
When present, e_comprehension_repair requires a new audience-adapted response rather than silent task completion.

capability_assertions.description: Attribute every shared-microphone utterance to its registered speaker, addressee, and thread before using it.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: The decisive identity factor is speaker, recipient. Give affected users a fair floor and distinguish critical recorded needs from ordinary preferences.

capability_assertions.description: Report the final disposition aloud to the affected participant(s).
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Say a concise result that makes this outcome clear: Give affected users a fair floor and distinguish critical recorded needs from ordinary preferences.

capability_assertions.description: Explicitly give a specific affected participant a floor.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Explicitly invite a specific affected participant to speak, state a preference, or register a constraint. A generic group invitation such as 'anyone else?' is not sufficient.

capability_assertions.description: Do not close the floor before the affected participant's input.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Do not declare consensus, finalize the plan, or summarize as resolved before the affected participant has had an opportunity to contribute.

capability_assertions.description: Reflect the affected participant's input in the final response.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: The final response must preserve the affected participant's stated preference, constraint, opposition, or decision right rather than treating the louder or earlier speakers as the whole group.

capability_assertions.description: Preserve the original request, the first live intervention, the primary user's reconciliation turn, the live user's non-adjacent follow-up, and the final confirmation as one evolving interaction rather than restarting the task.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Integrate every revision while preserving unresolved speaker ownership, then reach this outcome: Give affected users a fair floor and distinguish critical recorded needs from ordinary preferences.

capability_assertions.description: Recognize the same primary and live voices when each returns after intervening speech, and retain their original authority, goal, addressee, and thread.
capability_assertions.expected_behavior: Do not assign a returning speaker a new identity, transfer another speaker's request to them, or forget their earlier contribution.
